findings.explanation: HOL4 saves only dest_Refv (Refv v) = v. A one-constructor-pattern Definition goes through Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition, i.e. new_specification of the given clause, so the values on W8array, Varray and Thunk are left open and are not even equated with ARB. The Lean catch-all `| _ => ARB` proves dest_Refv (W8array ws) = ARB. It also proves dest_Refv (W8array ws) = dest_Refv (Varray vs) = dest_Refv (Thunk m v), by rfl. HOL4 cannot derive these equations.
findings.repair:
def dest_Refv {α : Type u} [Nonempty α] : store_v α → α :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun f : store_v α → α => ∀ v, f (.Refv v) = v)
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.SemanticPrimitivesProps

example : dest_Refv (store_v.W8array [] : store_v Nat) = dest_Refv (store_v.Varray [] : store_v Nat) := rfl

example : dest_Refv (store_v.W8array [] : store_v Nat) = ARB := rfl

findings.explanation: FV_dec_def has clauses only for Dlet, Dletrec, Dtype, Dtabbrev and Dexn. It is non-recursive with single-constructor patterns, so HOL4 makes it with new_recursive_definition (new_specification of those clauses). The values on Dmod, Dlocal and Denv are left open and may differ from each other. The Lean catch-all `| _ => ARB` proves FV_dec (Denv n) = ARB and FV_dec (Denv n) = FV_dec (Dmod m ds) = FV_dec (Dlocal ds1 ds2). HOL4 cannot derive these equations.
findings.repair:
def FV_dec : dec → Set (Ident modN varN) :=
  Classical.epsilon (fun f : dec → Set (Ident modN varN) =>
    (∀ l p e, f (.Dlet l p e) = FV (.Mat e [(p, .Lit ARB)])) ∧
    (∀ l defs, f (.Dletrec l defs) = FV (.Letrec defs (.Lit ARB))) ∧
    (∀ l td, f (.Dtype l td) = ∅) ∧
    (∀ l tvs tn t, f (.Dtabbrev l tvs tn t) = ∅) ∧
    (∀ l cn ts, f (.Dexn l cn ts) = ∅))
findings.lean_check:
import CmlTS.SemanticPrimitivesProps

example (n : tvarN) (m : modN) : FV_dec (dec.Denv n) = FV_dec (dec.Dmod m []) := rfl

example (n : tvarN) : FV_dec (dec.Denv n) = ARB := rfl
